newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley says drops some Mass. munibond work.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley says drops some Mass. munibond work.

text.p: Morgan Stanley & Co. said Monday it has pulled out of some Massachusetts municipal bond work because one of its top officials made a contribution to Massachusetts Gov. William Weld's Senate campaign, possibly in violation of political contribution regulations.

The firm said in a statement that it has withdrawn from any municipal securities business with Massachusetts and state authorities while the National Association of Securities Dealers reviews its request for a "waiver" from the rule's penalties in this instance.

The rule, enacted by the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) in April 1994, bars municipal dealers that make contributions to municipal bond issuers from doing business for two years with those governments.
Dealers must keep records of contributions and report quarterly to the board, the self-regulating agency for the municipal bond market. The next quarterly reports from firms are due on Oct. 31.
The board has stated in guidelines to municipal firms that the rule covers contributions to state and local issuer officials running for federal office.

A Morgan Stanley spokeswoman said, "During preparation of the firm's quarterly filing, it was discovered that a senior fixed income managing director had, without the firm's knowledge, made a political contribution in early September to the U.S. Senate campaign of Massachusetts Gov. William Weld."

The contributor assumed that contributions to federal, as opposed to state and local, political campaigns were not covered by the rule, known as G-37, or firm policies concerning the rule, Morgan Stanley said.

The firm said it has asked NASD for a waiver from rule G-37 in connection with the $1,000 contribution. The contribution "has been fully refunded to the contributor by the Weld campaign," the firm added.
The firm's statement did not say who made the contribution. The Wall Street Journal reported Monday the contribution was made by Peter Karches, head of Morgan Stanely's fixed-income department.

Morgan said until NASD decides on the waiver question, the firm has voluntarily chosen "to withdraw from any municipal securities business" with the state and any Massachusetts "entities that could be construed to be subject to Rule G-37."

Morgan said the firm's legal department notified federal regulators about the contribution on the day it was discovered. It said the official reported the contribution on an internal quarterly reporting form.
MSRB officials were not immediately available.
